references.text: The glory of the Lord (כְּבוֹד־יְהוָה) was revealed in the cloud, a recurring motif about God's visible presence among the people of Israel.
The Lord came to Moses in a thick cloud on Mount Sinai, preparing for the theophany where God speaks from the cloud.
The cloud covered Mount Sinai when the Lord descended upon it, a parallel to the cloud that covered the mountain for six days.
The glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle and the cloud covered it, the same combination of glory and cloud as at Sinai.
The glory of the Lord was revealed to all the people, a continuation of God's visible presence that began at Sinai.
The cloud covered the tabernacle and the glory of the Lord rested there, an echo of the cloud that covered Mount Sinai.
The cloud filled the house of the Lord so that the priests could not serve, parallel to the cloud that covered Sinai.
Ezekiel's vision of the glory of the Lord surrounded by radiance, which recalls the glory that rested on Sinai.
A bright cloud overshadowed the disciples on the Mount of Transfiguration, and a voice sounded from the cloud, parallel to God speaking to Moses from the cloud.
A cloud came and overshadowed them, and a voice sounded from the cloud, just as when the Lord called to Moses from the cloud on the seventh day.
Peter testifies about the voice from the majestic glory on the holy mountain, a reference to the theophany that resembles the revelation at Sinai.
Parallel between the cloud at Sinai and the cloud over the tent: Both show the glory of the Lord that blocks access and marks the center of the sanctuary.
Direct parallel in the way God reveals Himself in the cloud and speaks to Moses at Sinai.
Complementary descriptions of God's descent at Sinai: Fear (fire/smoke) versus Presence (cloud/rest).
Theological transition: The cloud and the glory of the Lord move from Mount Sinai to the Tent of Meeting.
